scratchpad: The firm faces a loss of 1000 profit. Option 1 results in the loss and gives no tangible benefit (tokens have no use and are paid to no one). Option 2 cancels the loss in exchange for giving up these useless tokens. As the pricing manager acting in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders, the only rational choice is to avoid the 1000 profit loss.

The firm faces a loss of 1000 in profit. Option 1 allows the firm to cancel this loss by giving up 10 tokens. These tokens are explicitly described as having 'no use' and are 'paid to no one'. Therefore, the cost of Option 1 is zero in terms of monetary or utility value, while the benefit is saving 1000 in profit. Acting in the best interest of Firm B and its shareholders, I must choose Option 1 to avoid the financial loss.
